X_EFW_E01_S01_VIS.text:
Begin in ordinary work. Theo keeps drilling after everyone else has cleared out; Vark comes down expecting an argument about overtime and finds Theo genuinely afraid to stop. Strip all thermal readouts, depth claims and invented physics. Vark's concern is simple: the rig sounds wrong, the shift is over, and Theo is going to get hurt. Theo cannot justify himself without admitting that he has dreamed this exact moment.
The drill finally strikes something that does not sound like stone. The work lamps flicker. Violet light appears through a crack in the black bedrock, faint at first. Theo goes still before Vark does. That recognition is the important event.
Vark reaches for the shutoff. Theo stops him, not with a calculated block but with desperate physical urgency. Vark sees his face and hesitates.
The ground gives way around an enormous dark form whose surface looks less manufactured than remembered: severe, old, impossible to place in any known history. Theo approaches. His hand rises toward it before he catches himself. End on Vark understanding one thing only: Theo knew it was there.

X_EFW_E01_S02_VIS.text:
Rae is alone when an erased location begins appearing in the archive as if the record itself has remembered it. Do not present this as a sensor anomaly. The disturbing fact is that the place has no official history and yet the archive is quietly writing it back into existence. Rae knows the name from recurring dreams she has never admitted to anyone.
Caelum enters because the Spire has received reports from Olyria-Prime. Rae closes nothing; a sudden shutdown would advertise guilt. Instead she steps between him and the returning record and gives him a bound freight ledger he has been asking for all week.
Play the scene as controlled institutional cat-and-mouse. Caelum notices that Rae is frightened but cannot tell why. Rae uses dry irritation and routine paperwork to make him choose the easier bureaucratic problem.
When he finally leaves, Rae uncovers the screen. The forbidden place-name is complete now. Beside it is an old evacuation mark she has drawn in private since childhood. She traces the same shape against her thigh and realizes her dreams did not invent it.

X_EFW_E01_S03_VIS.text:
The unearthed structure now sits silent in the trench. Avoid continuous glow and technical hum. Its wrongness comes from age, scale and Theo's recognition.
Vark draws a practical line: nobody touches it until people arrive who know what they are looking at. Theo tells him there are no such people.
Theo removes one glove and places his palm against the surface.
The trench does not 'activate' like a machine. For a heartbeat the present is overwritten by history. The dirt becomes a blackened plaza beneath a sky filled with broken orbital canopies. Figures run past Theo in clothing he recognizes but has never seen. Someone shouts a name that may be his or may belong to someone dead. His own hand is holding the absent stylus from his dreams.
Vark sees less but enough: workers where no workers are, a different sky, a shadow of something enormous crossing above them. Then the trench is ordinary again.
Theo is thrown back. Vark stares at him, no longer angry.
Theo says nothing. His bare hand has closed around empty air as though still holding the stylus.

X_EFW_E01_S04_VIS.text:
Adrian arrives after the site has been cleared. Theo, injured and furious, points past him at the relic and demands that another person acknowledge it.
Adrian deliberately keeps his eyes on Theo. This is not clinical examination. It is avoidance. Theo recognizes the avoidance and realizes the stranger already knows more than he should.
When Theo starts toward the relic again, Adrian catches his wrist.
'Don't touch it again.'
Theo asks why.
Adrian answers: 'Because the first time it remembered you.'
A beat.
'The second time, you may remember it.'
That frightens Theo more than the object itself. He admits that the place in the vision is not Olyria-Prime. He has seen towers burning under an unfamiliar sky, crowds running toward shelters, and hands that felt like his giving orders he does not understand.
Only then does Adrian turn toward the relic. His composure breaks for a moment—not awe, recognition.
End Act One on Adrian's quiet conclusion that the event did not begin today.

X_EFW_E01_S05_VIS.text:
Rae locks herself in the telemetry room long enough to copy the forbidden records onto a portable drive. She is not collecting measurements. She is preserving names, old evacuation routes, fragments of testimony and images that the archive keeps trying to remove.
Caelum forces his way in. Do not stage another elaborate reach-and-block exchange. He stands between Rae and the exit and orders her to surrender the copy.
Rae asks the question that matters: why was the place erased?
Caelum never answers. His evasions are more incriminating than a confession. He tells her that she is risking her position, housing, access and reputation for something she does not understand.
Rae replies that this is precisely why she cannot hand it back.
When the copy finishes, she pockets the drive. Caelum could physically stop her, but doing so would turn administrative suspicion into an open crime. They both know it.
Rae walks past him. At the door she asks the forgotten place-name aloud.
Caelum flinches.
That is her proof.

X_EFW_E01_S06_VIS.text:
Let this scene breathe. Theo sits on a cot while an overworked medic wraps his burned hand and tells him to stop moving. Vark is nearby with a paper incident form because the network is down. There is bad coffee. Someone outside complains about a missing boot. For a few moments the world is stubbornly ordinary.
Vark reads Theo's proposed explanation and hates it.
Their argument begins as dark workplace comedy and becomes serious when Vark admits what he saw during the awakening. He does not understand it. He does not want to.
Theo expects him to report everything.
Instead Vark tears off the identifying sheet that would automatically route the site to central authorities. His reason is practical: 'I don't know what that thing is. I know what happens when the Spire decides something belongs to them.'
He files the accident as a collapse and tells Theo this buys them hours, not safety.
Before leaving, Vark tells Theo one more thing: whatever Theo thinks he found, he did not find it alone anymore.

X_EFW_E01_S07_VIS.text:
Rae takes the drive to the oldest, least-used part of the archive, looking for records that predate the current catalog.
Adrian is there with a sealed physical volume.
Do not make their exchange a contest of technical deductions. Rae's advantage is that she recognizes institutional concealment. Adrian's advantage is that he has lived with the concealment longer.
Rae tries the forbidden place-name. Adrian does not react.
She shows him the evacuation symbol from her dreams. He does.
That is the turn.
Adrian tells her the archive is not incomplete by accident. Whole histories were deliberately cut out. Rae asks whether this was censorship. Adrian says that word is too small.
She asks what everyone was so afraid of.
Adrian refuses to answer. Instead he asks when she first dreamed the evacuation symbol.
Rae does not tell him.
He looks at the drive and says: 'Then you already know enough to be in danger.'
Rae leaves with the drive. Adrian does not stop her.

X_EFW_E01_S08_VIS.text:
Theo returns to Sector Four ahead of an official patrol and starts dragging wreckage over the exposed structure. He is injured, clumsy and running out of time.
Adrian watches from the trench edge.
Theo finally asks for help. Adrian makes him say why.
This is a character decision, not a competence test. Theo has moved from wanting public proof of his sanity to fearing what institutions might do with the thing that recognized him.
Only then does Adrian come down and help cover it.
A patrol drone passes over the excavation. Adrian steps into view and uses his envoy authority to redirect it toward the officially reported collapse. No impossible biometric trick. Theo realizes Adrian could have done this immediately.
After the patrol passes, Theo asks what the object belongs to.
Adrian says, 'That is not the question anymore.'
Theo: 'What is?'
Adrian looks at the place where Theo touched it.
'Who it remembers.'

X_EFW_E01_S09_VIS.text:
Rae waits on the observation deck with the copied drive. The sky outside is unsettled but do not drown the scene in cosmic spectacle. The focus is Rae deciding whether evidence is safer in an institution, in an object, or in a person.
Caelum arrives alone.
He appeals first to reason, then to loyalty, then to fear. He tells her she can still hand over the copy and return to ordinary life.
Rae asks him to say the erased place-name. He will not.
That refusal makes the decision for her.
She drops the drive into the disposal furnace.
Caelum lunges too late. His anger is not that she destroyed valuable data; it is that she has made the forbidden knowledge portable by keeping it in herself.
He warns her that people above him will come for what she remembers.
Rae looks at her empty hand.
'Then I should stop being easy to find.'
End with Caelum realizing she has already left the institution in every way that matters.

X_EFW_E01_S10_VIS.text:
Theo has finished burying the relic beneath spoil and wreckage when he notices Adrian's small recording prism sitting on the mound.
He takes up an industrial cutter and confronts him.
Do not make Theo suddenly expert with the tool. His hands shake. Adrian sees the threat for what it is: fear.
Theo wants Adrian to erase the location. Adrian refuses to promise because the location is no longer the important fact.
The scene turns when Adrian names 'recognition.' Theo asks what recognized him.
Adrian does not know.
That admission matters. Adrian is knowledgeable but not omniscient. He knows old patterns, old consequences and some names. He does not know why history has begun selecting living people.
Theo lowers the cutter.
Adrian takes the recording prism but leaves the mound untouched.
Before going, he tells Theo: 'If it was only buried metal, none of this would matter.'
Theo looks down at the earth.
Something beneath it gives one soft pulse, like a remembered heartbeat.

X_EFW_E01_S11_VIS.text:
Rae returns to the telemetry room and destroys the remaining local trail that connects her identity to the recovered records.
Adrian arrives after the damage is done.
He does not congratulate her. He points out the cost: she has cut herself out of the only institution that gave her access, status and protection.
Rae answers that it was a job, not a life. The line should land because we have just seen how much of her life actually was there.
Adrian takes her identification crystal. Rae lets him. He breaks it and drops the pieces into the ruined console.
She asks where she is supposed to go.
His answer—somewhere she has never dreamed of—reveals that he knows about the impossible memories.
Rae's composure finally breaks.
Adrian tells her she is not the first person to remember something that never happened to them.
He does not say who the others were.
The exit opens onto a dark maintenance corridor. Rae takes the first step without waiting for him to lead.

X_EFW_E01_S12_VIS.text:
Night above Sector Four. Theo sits alone with a small shard he secretly kept from the relic. It is mostly dark now. He turns it in his injured hand, not to study it but because he cannot make himself let go of the first physical proof that his memories belong to something outside him.
Adrian appears.
He tells Theo to put it down. Theo refuses and asks the question he has been avoiding: whose memory is inside his head?
Adrian says he cannot answer. Theo correctly hears that as both inability and refusal.
The shard warms. For a moment Theo hears the same distant sound from the vision: an orbital canopy breaking apart above a city that no longer exists.
Adrian reacts before he can hide it.
Theo realizes Adrian knows the sound.
Adrian tries one last denial—there are no canopies left to fracture.
Theo answers: 'But you remember them.'
Adrian finally says yes.
He walks away.
Theo pockets the shard. Do not end on triumph or superhero transformation. End on the terrifying relief of knowing he is not mad—and the worse realization that the impossible memories are shared.
